sentence: This project studies in mice how a shortened gene leads to two brain malformations that are linked to epilepsy and autism.
This project measures how people differ in cancer-relevant gene mutations in bronchial cells, and compares this with age, smoking and lung cancer.
This project builds a chip model of the temporomandibular joint to study how its different tissues communicate with each other.
This project studies why B-cell lymphoma resists a drug that blocks protein arginine methyltransferase, using mouse models and human lymphoma.
This project studies how a protein on the surface of chimeric antigen receptor T cells affects how well the cells work and last.
This project designs nanobodies that work against the virus causing COVID-19 and related coronaviruses, guided by protein structure.
This project develops statistical methods that combine genetic variation, gene expression and epigenetics data to find genes involved in disease.
This project studies whether hydrogen sulfide helps stem cells protect the intestine in necrotizing enterocolitis, using a hydrogen sulfide probe and mice.
This project tries to increase clinical trial enrollment in gynecologic cancer by matching patients to targeted therapies at the molecular level.
This project runs a facility that provides instruments and expertise for flow cytometry and single cell analysis in biomedical research.
This project studies why children with chronic cholestatic liver disease develop sarcopenia, looking at muscle mitochondria, oxidative stress, protein metabolism and bile acids.
This project studies how tumors and immune cells interact during treatment, using biopsies, image analysis and mathematical modeling.
This project develops a method to purify DNA and RNA from preserved tissue samples so that high quality DNA sequencing is possible.
This project shares imaging software and hardware tools, large imaging datasets and tools for using imaging technology in clinical workflows.
This project records the lineage and signaling history of cells in skin organoids with spatial sequencing to find what drives clonal competition.
This project studies whether sulfites in the diet interfere with normal colon function in health and in ulcerative colitis.
This project builds a head-mounted miniature mesoscope that records activity across the cortex of freely behaving mice during social interactions.
This project develops a noninvasive way to diagnose and monitor small-vessel coronary dysfunction using magnetic resonance imaging.
This project builds a 3D super-resolution mapping technology to watch cavitation activity in real time during laser lithotripsy for urinary stone disease.
